summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of possible mast cell degranulation syndrome was admitted for chest, abdominal, leg, and back pain, along with diarrhea and constipation, which she attributed to a mast cell flare triggered by a UTI. She had started ciprofloxacin from her PCP but was unable to fill the initial prescription due to cost. In the ED, she had lower abdominal tenderness and a positive urinalysis; CT abdomen/pelvis showed no acute pathology. She was treated with IV dilaudid, benadryl, and ativan per her flare protocol and continued on ciprofloxacin. Urine culture grew E. coli resistant to ciprofloxacin, prompting a post-discharge call to switch to nitrofurantoin. The patient declined psychiatric evaluation, though her presentation included elements of complex chronic pain and possible somatic symptom concerns. She was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments, including new prescriptions for fexofenadine and topiramate, and a follow-up appointment with a new allergist.
